description:
The deployment-tunable surface of ``dataset/pii_scan`` (ADR-0068/0070) — the
scan bound + backend. **Operational** scope (the default): a workflow or run may
tune these freely (unlike a governance gate threshold). A subset of ``PiiInput``;
the safe defaults live on ``PiiInput`` so an un-configured run is still bounded.

preset.description:
Pick a ready-made configuration, then override individual settings below if needed.
• governed (default) — spaCy NER + regex + secret detection. Finds names, locations, emails, phones, cards, API keys. Best recall; ~7 min / 200k rows on a 2-CPU box, ~550 MB RAM.
• logs — regex + secrets only, NO name/location detection (NER off). ~30% faster and ~200 MB RAM. Use for logs, traces, and incident data where there are no personal names to catch.
preset.title: PII scan mode

ner.description: Run the spaCy language model to catch PERSON, LOCATION, and ORGANIZATION — the PII that has no fixed pattern. Turn OFF for regex + secrets only: much faster and lighter, but names and places will NOT be found. Leave ON for training data; turning it off is only safe for structured/log data.
ner.title: Detect names & locations (NER)

model.description:
Which spaCy model powers name/location detection (ignored when NER is off).
• sm (small, default) — fast, ~550 MB RAM, misses ~1-2% of names. Best fit for a small (2-CPU) box.
• lg (large) — highest recall, ~1.2-1.7 GB RAM, same speed. Use where RAM is plentiful and you need to catch every name.
• blank — tokenizer only, no NER at all (same as turning NER off).
model.title: Language model

n_process.description: How many CPU workers share the detection pass. 0 = auto (use all available cores) — recommended. On a 2-CPU box this is ~40% faster than a single worker. Set to 1 to force single-process (lowest RAM, e.g. when the box also runs other heavy services). Values above the core count are capped automatically.
n_process.title: Parallel workers

analyze_chunk.description: How many rows are fed to the detector at once. Larger batches let the parallel workers stay busy (needed for 'Parallel workers' to help); smaller batches use less memory. 2048 is a good balance — you rarely need to change this.
analyze_chunk.title: Rows per batch

sample_size.description: For a go/no-go readiness verdict the scan checks a random sample rather than every row, so cost stays flat no matter how large the dataset. 1000 is a statistically sound default. Raise it for a tighter estimate; set to blank (null) to scan every single row (slower on big datasets). Note: redaction (the fix step) always processes every row — sampling applies to the CHECK only.
sample_size.title: Rows to sample

backend.description: Detector engine: 'auto' (cascade when presidio is installed, else regex) covers almost every case. Advanced: 'cascade' (regex-in-presidio, ADR-0079), 'presidio', 'regex' (zero-dep), 'regexset' ([fastpii] re2).
backend.title: PII backend

secrets_full_scan.description: Scan every row for leaked credentials (API keys, tokens, private keys) even when name/PII detection is sampled — a rare secret would slip past a sample. Recommended on; turn off only for a pure sampled density estimate.
secrets_full_scan.title: Full-corpus secret scan

title: PiiScanConfig
